content.substance.CIGARETTES.name: Cigarettes
content.milestone.heart-rate.title: Heart rate settles
content.milestone.heart-rate.description: Heart rate and blood pressure start dropping back towards normal.
content.milestone.oxygen.title: Oxygen recovers
content.milestone.oxygen.description: Carbon monoxide in your blood halves and oxygen levels climb back to normal.
content.milestone.carbon-monoxide.title: Carbon monoxide cleared
content.milestone.carbon-monoxide.descri: Carbon monoxide in your blood drops to a normal level.
content.milestone.taste-smell.title: Taste & smell wake up
content.milestone.taste-smell.descriptio: Damaged nerve endings start to regrow; food tastes and smells better.
content.milestone.nicotine-free.title: Nicotine-free body
content.milestone.nicotine-free.descript: Nicotine has left your body. Withdrawal usually peaks now — it gets easier from here.
content.milestone.breathing.title: Easier breathing
content.milestone.breathing.description: Bronchial tubes relax and energy levels rise.
content.milestone.withdrawal-fades.title: Withdrawal fading
content.milestone.withdrawal-fades.descr: Most physical withdrawal symptoms have faded; brain nicotine receptors are normalising.
content.milestone.circulation.title: Circulation & lungs up
content.milestone.circulation.descriptio: Circulation has improved and lung function has increased by up to 10%.
content.milestone.cilia.title: Lungs self-cleaning
content.milestone.cilia.description: Coughing and shortness of breath decrease; lung cilia work normally again.
content.milestone.heart-disease-half.des: Excess risk of coronary heart disease is about half that of a smoker.
content.milestone.stroke.title: Stroke risk lowered
content.milestone.stroke.description: Stroke risk can fall to that of a non-smoker; mouth, throat and bladder cancer risk halves.
content.milestone.lung-cancer-half.title: Lung cancer risk halved
content.milestone.lung-cancer-half.descr: Risk of dying from lung cancer is about half that of a person who still smokes.
content.milestone.heart-like-nonsmoker.d: Risk of coronary heart disease is the same as someone who never smoked.
content.substance.ROLL_YOUR_OWN.name: Roll-your-own
content.substance.CIGARS.name: Cigars
content.substance.VAPE.name: Vape
content.substance.HEATED_TOBACCO.name: Heated tobacco
content.substance.ALCOHOL.name: Alcohol
content.milestone.alc-withdrawal-peak.de: Physical withdrawal usually peaks 24–72 hours after the last drink, then eases. Shaking, confusion or seeing things still need urgent medical help.
content.milestone.alc-sleep.title: Sleep starts to recover
content.milestone.alc-sleep.description: Without alcohol fragmenting it, deep and REM sleep begin to return; most people sleep better within a week or two.
content.milestone.alc-month.title: Liver, blood pressure & blood sugar improve
content.milestone.alc-month.description: In a study of a month without alcohol, liver fat, blood pressure and insulin resistance all dropped (Mehta et al., BMJ Open 2018).
content.milestone.alc-mood.title: Mood steadies
content.milestone.alc-mood.description: Anxiety and low mood caused by drinking often lift within weeks to months of stopping.
content.milestone.alc-liver-year.title: Liver given a full year
content.milestone.alc-liver-year.descrip: Fatty liver from drinking is usually reversible. A year alcohol-free gives your liver its best chance (scarring from cirrhosis doesn't reverse).
content.milestone.alc-cancer.title: Cancer risk keeps falling
content.milestone.alc-cancer.description: Risk of alcohol-related cancers (mouth, throat, oesophagus, liver, breast, bowel) declines the longer you stay stopped.
content.safety.heavy-daily-drinker-don-t: Heavy daily drinker? Don't stop alone

Stopping suddenly after heavy daily drinking can cause seizures or delirium tremens, which can be fatal. Talk to a doctor about a supervised detox or taper. Get emergency help for shaking you can't control, confusion, seizures or hallucinations.
content.safety.don-t-mix-depressants.bod: Combining opioids, benzodiazepines, alcohol or other sedatives multiplies the risk of breathing stopping.
content.safety.if-it-gets-dark.title: If it gets dark
content.safety.if-it-gets-dark.body: Low mood is common in early recovery. If you have thoughts of suicide, call your local crisis line (988 in the US, 116 123 Samaritans in the UK and Ireland) or emergency services.
content.substance.CANNABIS.name: Cannabis
content.milestone.can-start.title: Withdrawal begins
content.milestone.can-start.description: Irritability, restlessness and trouble sleeping often start within a day or two. They're temporary.
content.milestone.can-peak.title: Past the peak
content.milestone.can-peak.description: Cannabis withdrawal usually peaks between days 2 and 6, then fades.
content.milestone.can-two-weeks.title: Withdrawal mostly over
content.milestone.can-two-weeks.descript: Most withdrawal symptoms are gone within about two weeks; vivid dreams and sleep changes can last a little longer.
content.milestone.can-receptors.title: Brain receptors reset
content.milestone.can-receptors.descript: Cannabinoid (CB1) receptors, reduced by regular use, return to normal levels after about four weeks (Hirvonen et al., Molecular Psychiatry 2012).
content.milestone.can-memory.title: Sharper memory
content.milestone.can-memory.description: Memory and attention measurably improve within a month of stopping (Schuster et al., J Clin Psychiatry 2018).
content.milestone.can-sleep.title: Sleep settles
content.milestone.can-sleep.description: Sleep without cannabis usually feels normal again within about a month or two.
content.milestone.can-year.title: One year free
content.milestone.can-year.description: A year of new routines, clearer mornings and money kept.
content.safety.get-help-for-unusual-thou: If you notice paranoia, hearing voices or thoughts that feel very out of character, talk to a doctor promptly.
content.substance.OPIOIDS.name: Opioids
content.milestone.op-peak.title: Through the peak
content.milestone.op-peak.description: Withdrawal from short-acting opioids like heroin usually peaks on days 1–3. Withdrawal from methadone starts later and lasts longer.
content.milestone.op-acute-over.title: Acute withdrawal fading
content.milestone.op-acute-over.descript: Physical symptoms from short-acting opioids usually ease within 5–10 days.
content.milestone.op-sleep.title: Sleep & appetite return
content.milestone.op-sleep.description: Sleep, appetite and energy keep improving over the following weeks.
content.milestone.op-reward.title: Reward system recovering
content.milestone.op-reward.description: Low mood, anxiety and cravings can come in waves for months (post-acute withdrawal). They get further apart.
content.milestone.op-year.title: One year in recovery
content.milestone.op-year.description: Every month in recovery makes the next one more likely. Medication like methadone or buprenorphine counts as recovery too.
content.safety.your-tolerance-drops-fast: After even a few days without opioids, an amount you used to take can stop your breathing. If you use again: use far less, never use alone, keep naloxone (Narcan) nearby, and call emergency services (112 / 911) if someone can't be woken or is breathing slowly.
content.safety.signs-of-an-overdose.body: Tiny pupils, slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips and fingertips, gurgling or snoring sounds, can't be woken. Call emergency services, give naloxone if you have it, and put the person in the recovery position.
content.substance.STIMULANTS.name: Stimulants (cocaine, meth, speed)
content.milestone.st-crash.title: The crash passes
content.milestone.st-crash.description: The first days often bring exhaustion, hunger and low mood. It's the body recovering, and it passes.
content.milestone.st-withdrawal.title: Withdrawal easing
content.milestone.st-withdrawal.descript: Fatigue, low mood and strong cravings usually ease over one to two weeks (longer after methamphetamine).
content.milestone.st-sleep.title: Sleep & appetite normalise
content.milestone.st-sleep.description: Sleep and eating patterns settle back into a rhythm.
content.milestone.st-mood.title: Joy coming back
content.milestone.st-mood.description: Flat mood (anhedonia) can last weeks to months, then lifts as the brain's reward system heals.
content.milestone.st-dopamine.title: Dopamine system recovered
content.milestone.st-dopamine.descriptio: After about 14 months without methamphetamine, dopamine transporter levels recovered substantially (Volkow et al., J Neurosci 2001).
content.safety.drug-supply-can-contain-f: Cocaine and meth are increasingly cut with fentanyl. If you use again: never alone, test with fentanyl strips if you can, and keep naloxone nearby.
content.substance.BENZODIAZEPINES.name: Benzodiazepines
content.milestone.bz-early.title: Early withdrawal window
content.milestone.bz-early.description: Symptoms start within 1–2 days for short-acting benzos and up to a week for long-acting ones.
content.milestone.bz-acute.title: Acute withdrawal fading
content.milestone.bz-acute.description: Acute withdrawal often lasts two to four weeks after the last dose.
content.milestone.bz-sleep.title: Sleep & calm improving
content.milestone.bz-sleep.description: Sleep and anxiety keep improving; some people have lingering symptoms for months, which do fade.
content.milestone.bz-year.title: One year free
content.safety.never-stop-benzos-suddenl: Stopping suddenly after regular use can cause seizures. Reduce slowly with a doctor's taper plan. Get emergency help for seizures, confusion or hallucinations.
content.substance.KRATOM.name: Kratom
content.milestone.kr-peak.title: Through the peak
content.milestone.kr-peak.description: Kratom withdrawal resembles mild opioid withdrawal and usually peaks within the first three days.
content.milestone.kr-acute.title: Acute withdrawal fading
content.milestone.kr-acute.description: Most physical symptoms ease within about a week.
content.milestone.kr-month.title: Energy & sleep return
content.milestone.kr-month.description: Sleep and energy keep improving over the following weeks.
content.milestone.kr-year.title: One year free
content.substance.GAMBLING.name: Gambling
content.milestone.b-day-one.title: First day back in control
content.milestone.b-day-one.description: One full day of choosing differently. That's the hardest one.
content.milestone.b-urges-peak.title: First urge wave ridden out
content.milestone.b-urges-peak.descripti: Urges are often strongest in the first days; each one you ride out weakens the habit loop.
content.milestone.b-week.title: A week of new routines
content.milestone.b-week.description: Your days have new shapes now. Notice what you're doing with the time and energy you got back.
content.milestone.b-month.title: Habit loop weakening
content.milestone.b-month.description: Around a month in, many people notice urges come less often and fade faster.
content.milestone.b-90.title: Ninety days
content.milestone.b-90.description: A classic recovery milestone: new routines are becoming automatic.
content.milestone.b-year.title: One year free
content.milestone.b-year.description: A full year of choosing yourself. Lapses get rarer the longer you go.
content.safety.make-gambling-harder-to-r: Self-exclude from betting sites and venues, install a gambling blocker, and let someone you trust help manage money for a while.

content.substance.CAFFEINE.name: Caffeine
content.milestone.caf-peak.title: Headache peak passing
content.milestone.caf-peak.description: Caffeine withdrawal headaches and tiredness peak 20–51 hours after the last cup (Juliano & Griffiths 2004).
content.milestone.caf-over.title: Withdrawal over
content.milestone.caf-sleep.title: Deeper sleep
content.milestone.caf-sleep.description: Without late caffeine, falling asleep and deep sleep usually improve.
content.milestone.caf-energy.title: Natural energy
content.milestone.caf-energy.description: Your energy now comes without the mid-afternoon crash.
content.substance.SUGAR.name: Sugar
content.milestone.sug-cravings.title: First cravings ridden out
content.milestone.sug-cravings.descripti: Cravings are often strongest in the first few days.
content.milestone.sug-energy.title: Steadier energy
content.milestone.sug-energy.description: Without sugar spikes, energy through the day tends to even out.
content.milestone.sug-taste.title: Taste adjusting
content.milestone.sug-taste.description: Many people find naturally sweet foods taste sweeter after a few weeks.
content.milestone.sug-month.title: New habits
content.milestone.sug-month.description: The after-dinner sweet reflex is fading.
content.substance.OTHER.name: Something else
content.prep.set-date.title: Set your quit date
content.prep.set-date.hint: Pick a day within the next two weeks — not a high-stress one.
content.prep.add-why.title: Write down your why
content.prep.add-why.hint: Add at least three reasons. You'll see them in every craving.
content.prep.tell-people.title: Tell friends & family
content.prep.tell-people.hint: Ask for support and add one person to call in an emergency.
content.prep.know-triggers.title: Know your triggers
content.prep.know-triggers.hint: Coffee, alcohol, after meals, stress? Plan a swap for each.
content.prep.get-aid.title: Line up medication or support
content.prep.get-aid.hint: Nicotine replacement, addiction medication, therapy and support groups each substantially improve your odds. Ask a doctor or pharmacist.
content.prep.clean-sweep.title: Clear it out
content.prep.clean-sweep.hint: Remove whatever you use, and the things you use it with, from home, car, bags and phone.
content.prep.plan-reward.title: Plan your first reward
content.prep.plan-reward.hint: Pick something your first week of savings will buy.
content.prep.save-quitline.title: Save a helpline number
content.prep.save-quitline.hint: Free expert support, one tap away in the SOS screen.

content.program.QUIT_VAPING.name: Quit vaping in 30 days
content.program.QUIT_VAPING.summary: A week to prepare, a quit day, then three weeks of support to stay vape-free.
content.program.QUIT_VAPING.evidence: Our own content, inspired by the phase-based approach (prepare, quit, stay quit) of text-message quit-vaping programs, which improved quit rates in a randomized trial with young adults (Graham AL et al., JAMA Intern Med 2021;181(7):923-30). Not affiliated with Truth Initiative.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-01.title: Write down your why
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-01.body: List three reasons you want to stop vaping. Keep the list on your phone's lock screen or somewhere you'll see it often.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-02.title: Notice when you vape
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-02.body: Today, just notice each time you reach for your vape. What were you doing and feeling?
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-03.title: Pick your quit day
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-03.body: Choose a day within the next week. A calmer day, without big deadlines or parties, makes the start easier.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-04.title: Tell someone you trust
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-04.body: Let a friend or family member know your quit day. Ask them to check in on you that week.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-05.title: Plan for your top trigger
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-05.body: Pick the moment you vape most and decide what you'll do instead, like a walk, gum or a glass of water.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-06.title: Talk to a pharmacist
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-06.body: Nicotine patches, gum or lozenges can take the edge off cravings. A pharmacist or doctor can help you choose.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-07.title: Clear out your gear
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-07.body: Tonight, throw away pods, chargers and spare devices. Fewer reminders mean fewer decisions tomorrow.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-08.title: Quit day is here
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-08.body: Today you don't vape. When a craving hits, remember it peaks and passes within a few minutes.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-09.title: Ride out a craving
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-09.body: When an urge comes, breathe slowly in for four and out for six until it fades. Log how long it lasted.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-10.title: Change one routine
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-10.body: Shift a habit linked to vaping, like taking a different route or having tea instead of coffee.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-11.title: Move your body
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-11.body: Ten minutes of brisk walking can cut cravings and lift your mood.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-12.title: Expect some grumpiness
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-12.body: Irritability and poor sleep are normal in the first weeks. They are signs your brain is adjusting.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-13.title: Two weeks: reward yourself
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-13.body: Spend some of the money you've saved on something that makes you smile.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-14.title: Handle social pressure
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-14.body: Practise a simple line, like "No thanks, I've stopped." Saying it out loud first makes it easier.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-15.title: Look after your sleep
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-15.body: Keep a regular bedtime and cut caffeine after lunch. Better sleep means fewer cravings.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-16.title: Three weeks strong
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-16.body: Look back at your logged cravings. Notice how they've become shorter or less frequent.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-17.title: Plan for a slip
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-17.body: If you vape once, it doesn't undo your progress. Decide now what you'll do to get straight back on track.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-18.title: Help someone else
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-18.body: Share one tip that worked for you with someone who's thinking about quitting.
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-19.title: Thirty days vape-free
content.mission.QUIT_VAPING.qv-19.body: Celebrate. Write down what helped most so you can come back to it if things get hard.
content.program.DAILY_MISSIONS.name: 30 daily missions
content.program.DAILY_MISSIONS.summary: One small, doable mission a day for your first month nicotine-free.
content.program.DAILY_MISSIONS.evidence: Daily missions in the style of the Smoke Free app, whose daily missions were linked to higher quit rates in an exploratory randomized trial (Crane D et al., F1000Research 2018;7:1524).
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-01.tit: Drink a big glass of water
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-01.bod: Water helps with dry mouth and gives your hands something to do.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-02.bod: Next time you crave, breathe in through your nose and out slowly through your mouth, five times.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-03.bod: When a craving comes, wait ten minutes before deciding anything. It will usually pass.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-04.bod: Walk for ten minutes. Moving is one of the quickest ways to ease an urge.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-05.bod: Check how much money you've kept so far and pick something to spend it on.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-06.bod: Wash your car, jacket or the corner where you used to smoke, so it smells fresh.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-07.bod: Share your first week with someone who will cheer you on.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-08.bod: Keep fruit, nuts or carrot sticks nearby for when your hands get restless.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-09.bod: If coffee and nicotine go together, try tea or change where you take your break.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-10.bod: Write down the situation that tempted you most today and one way to handle it next time.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-11.bod: Put on a song you love when a craving starts and let it carry you through.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-12.bod: Gentle stretching releases tension that can feel like a craving.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-13.bod: Write a short note about how you feel today to read on a hard day.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-14.bod: Use some of your savings on something small that feels good.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-15.bod: Pay attention to how food tastes and how things smell. They are already improving.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-16.bod: Carry a stress ball, pen or fidget toy to hold when the old habit kicks in.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-17.bod: Fill a risky time slot with something you enjoy, like cooking, a call or a film.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-18.bod: Step outside and take a few deep breaths. Notice how your lungs feel.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-19.bod: Practise turning down an offer, out loud or in your head, before you need to.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-20.bod: Good sleep makes cravings weaker. Aim for 30 minutes earlier tonight.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-21.bod: Read your craving log. Notice which tricks worked best for you.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-22.bod: Do one small new thing today. New routines help you leave old ones behind.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-23.bod: Send a message to someone who has helped you this month.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-24.bod: Notice your breathing, energy and skin. Write down one change you've felt.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-25.bod: Decide what you'll do if you slip, so one puff stays one puff.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-26.bod: Walk, cycle, dance or swim. Exercise helps your mood and your lungs.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-27.bod: Tell someone else who is quitting one thing that worked for you.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-28.bod: Add up the money and time you've kept this month.
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-29.bod: Imagine yourself a month from now, still nicotine-free. What will be different?
content.mission.DAILY_MISSIONS.dm-30.bod: You did it. Plan a proper treat and keep going one day at a time.
content.program.DRY_MONTH.name: Dry month
content.program.DRY_MONTH.summary: 31 days alcohol-free, with a mission most days to keep you going.
content.program.DRY_MONTH.evidence: Taking part in a month off alcohol was followed by less drinking six months later (de Visser RO, Robinson E, Bond R, Health Psychol 2016;35(3):281-9).
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-01.title: Set your intention
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-01.body: Write down why you're taking a month off drinking and what you hope to notice.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-02.title: Stock your fridge
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-02.body: Buy alcohol-free drinks you enjoy, like sparkling water, kombucha or alcohol-free beer.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-03.title: Tell your people
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-03.body: Let friends know you're having a dry month, so they can support rather than tempt you.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-04.title: Plan your evenings
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-04.body: Pick something for the evenings you'd usually drink, like a class, film or walk.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-05.title: Notice your sleep
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-05.body: Write down how you slept. Many people sleep more deeply within the first week.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-06.title: One week: reward yourself
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-06.body: Put the money you'd have spent on drinks towards something you enjoy.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-07.title: Order alcohol-free out
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-07.body: Next time you're out, order a non-alcoholic drink. Having a glass in hand helps.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-08.title: Ride out an urge
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-08.body: When you want a drink, wait 15 minutes and do something else. Notice how the urge fades.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-09.title: Find your Friday ritual
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-09.body: Replace the end-of-week drink with a new treat, like a bath, takeaway or long call.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-10.title: Two weeks: check in
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-10.body: How are your energy, mood and skin? Write down one change you've noticed.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-11.title: Practise saying no
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-11.body: Have a simple answer ready, such as "I'm not drinking this month." You don't owe anyone more.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-12.title: Move more
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-12.body: Use your extra energy for a run, swim or long walk.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-13.title: Spot your triggers
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-13.body: Notice which times, people or feelings make you want a drink most.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-14.title: Three weeks: look back
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-14.body: Read your notes. What's been easier than you expected?
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-15.title: Plan a sober social
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-15.body: Arrange a meet-up that isn't built around drinking, like brunch, a gig or a hike.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-16.title: Think about after
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-16.body: Decide how you want to drink, or not, when the month ends.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-17.title: Write your learnings
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-17.body: Note three things you learned about yourself and alcohol this month.
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-18.title: You did a dry month
content.mission.DRY_MONTH.dry-18.body: Celebrate. If you decide to drink again, starting slowly is safest.
content.program.T_BREAK.name: Tolerance break
content.program.T_BREAK.summary: Four weeks off cannabis, long enough for your brain's receptors to reset.
content.program.T_BREAK.evidence: Brain CB1 cannabinoid receptors, reduced in daily users, recovered to normal levels after about four weeks of abstinence (Hirvonen J et al., Mol Psychiatry 2012;17:642-9).
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-01.title: Set your break goal
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-01.body: Write down why you're taking a break and what you'd like to feel at the end.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-02.title: Put it out of reach
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-02.body: Give away or lock up your cannabis and gear, so it's not there when an urge hits.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-03.title: Prepare for sleep changes
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-03.body: Vivid dreams and restless nights are common early on. A regular bedtime helps.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-04.title: Eat regular meals
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-04.body: Appetite can dip for a few days. Small, regular meals keep your energy steady.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-05.title: Move every day
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-05.body: Exercise eases irritability and helps you sleep.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-06.title: One week: check in
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-06.body: Symptoms usually peak in the first week. Notice what's already easing.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-07.title: Fill your evenings
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-07.body: Plan something for the time you'd usually use, like a game, a call or cooking.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-08.title: Name your feelings
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-08.body: When you feel irritable or low, name the feeling. Naming it makes it easier to manage.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-09.title: Halfway there
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-09.body: Two weeks done. Spend some saved money on something that feels good.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-10.title: Notice the clarity
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-10.body: Write down one thing that feels clearer, like memory, focus or motivation.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-11.title: Three weeks strong
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-11.body: Most physical symptoms have usually passed by now. Keep going.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-12.title: Decide what's next
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-12.body: Think about how you want to use cannabis, if at all, after the break.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-13.title: Plan a lower-risk return
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-13.body: If you go back, use less, less often and lower strength. Your tolerance is lower now.
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-14.title: Break complete
content.mission.T_BREAK.tb-14.body: Four weeks is about how long brain cannabinoid receptors take to recover. Well done.
content.program.SKILL_LESSONS.name: Recovery skills
content.program.SKILL_LESSONS.summary: Eight short lessons in proven coping skills, one every two days.
content.program.SKILL_LESSONS.evidence: Based on cognitive behavioural therapy and the Community Reinforcement Approach, both effective for substance use (Magill M, Ray LA, J Stud Alcohol Drugs 2009; Meyers RJ, Roozen HG, Smith JE, Alcohol Res Health 2011).
content.mission.SKILL_LESSONS.sk-01.body: Think of a recent time you used. Write what happened before, what you felt, and what you got out of it. Patterns show you where to plan.
content.mission.SKILL_LESSONS.sk-02.body: Cravings rise, peak and fall like a wave, usually within minutes. Next time, notice where you feel it in your body and breathe until it passes.
content.mission.SKILL_LESSONS.sk-03.body: Look the person in the eye, say no clearly, and suggest something else to do. Rehearse it out loud so it comes easily.
content.mission.SKILL_LESSONS.sk-04.body: Choices that seem unimportant, like a shortcut past a shop, can lead you towards using. Pick one and make a safer choice.
content.mission.SKILL_LESSONS.sk-05.body: Name a problem that pulls you towards using. List three possible fixes, pick one and try it this week.
content.mission.SKILL_LESSONS.sk-06.body: Thoughts like "just one won't hurt" feel convincing. Write the thought down, then write a calmer, truer reply.
content.mission.SKILL_LESSONS.sk-07.body: Recovery sticks when life without using feels good. Schedule one enjoyable, healthy activity for each day this week.
content.mission.SKILL_LESSONS.sk-08.body: Write your warning signs, your top three coping steps and two people you'll call. Keep it somewhere you can find quickly.
content.assessment.AUDIT.name: AUDIT
content.assessment.AUDIT.purpose: A 10-question check of how drinking is affecting you, developed by the World Health Organization.
content.assessment.AUDIT.band0.label: Lower risk
content.assessment.AUDIT.band0.descripti: Your answers suggest a lower-risk drinking pattern.
content.assessment.AUDIT.band1.label: Increasing risk
content.assessment.AUDIT.band1.descripti: Your answers suggest drinking at a level that can raise health risks. Cutting down is likely to help.
content.assessment.AUDIT.band2.label: Higher risk
content.assessment.AUDIT.band2.descripti: Your answers suggest drinking that may already be causing harm. This is not a diagnosis. Talking it through with a doctor or support service can help you decide what to do next.
content.assessment.AUDIT.band3.label: Highest risk
content.assessment.AUDIT.band3.descripti: Your answers suggest you could benefit from professional support. This is not a diagnosis. Talking it through with a doctor or support service can help you decide what to do next.
content.assessment.AUDIT_C.name: AUDIT-C
content.assessment.AUDIT_C.purpose: The first three AUDIT questions: a quick look at how often and how much you drink.
content.assessment.AUDIT_C.band0.label: Lower risk
content.assessment.AUDIT_C.band0.descrip: Your answers suggest a lower-risk drinking pattern.
content.assessment.AUDIT_C.band1.label: Increasing risk
content.assessment.AUDIT_C.band1.descrip: Your answers suggest drinking that may raise health risks. Some services use 3 or more as the threshold for women. The full AUDIT gives a fuller picture.
content.assessment.HSI.name: Heaviness of Smoking Index
content.assessment.HSI.purpose: Two questions about how soon and how much you smoke, used to gauge nicotine dependence.
content.assessment.HSI.band0.label: Lower dependence
content.assessment.HSI.band0.description: Your answers suggest lower nicotine dependence.
content.assessment.HSI.band1.label: Moderate dependence
content.assessment.HSI.band1.description: Nicotine replacement or other quit aids may make withdrawal easier.
content.assessment.HSI.band2.label: Higher dependence
content.assessment.HSI.band2.description: Stop-smoking medicines and support roughly double your chances. This is not a diagnosis. Talking it through with a doctor or support service can help you decide what to do next.
content.assessment.CUDIT_R.name: CUDIT-R
content.assessment.CUDIT_R.purpose: Eight questions about how cannabis use is affecting you.
content.assessment.CUDIT_R.band0.label: Lower risk
content.assessment.CUDIT_R.band0.descrip: Your answers suggest a lower-risk pattern of use.
content.assessment.CUDIT_R.band1.label: Increasing risk
content.assessment.CUDIT_R.band1.descrip: Your answers suggest use that may be causing some harm.
content.assessment.CUDIT_R.band2.label: Higher risk
content.assessment.CUDIT_R.band2.descrip: Your answers suggest you could benefit from support. This is not a diagnosis. Talking it through with a doctor or support service can help you decide what to do next.
content.assessment.PGSI.name: Problem Gambling Severity Index
content.assessment.PGSI.purpose: Nine questions about how gambling has affected you over the last 12 months.
content.assessment.PGSI.band0.label: No signs of harm
content.assessment.PGSI.band0.descriptio: Your answers show no signs of gambling harm.
content.assessment.PGSI.band1.label: Lower risk
content.assessment.PGSI.band1.descriptio: Your answers suggest a low level of gambling harm.
content.assessment.PGSI.band2.label: Moderate risk
content.assessment.PGSI.band2.descriptio: Your answers suggest gambling is causing some harm. Blocking tools can help.
content.assessment.PGSI.band3.label: Higher risk
content.assessment.PGSI.band3.descriptio: Your answers suggest gambling is causing significant harm. This is not a diagnosis. Talking it through with a doctor or support service can help you decide what to do next.
content.assessment.BARC_10.name: Brief Assessment of Recovery Capital
content.assessment.BARC_10.purpose: Ten statements about the strengths and resources that support your recovery.
content.assessment.BARC_10.band0.label: Building recovery capital
content.assessment.BARC_10.band0.descrip: You have room to grow the supports around you. Small steps such as one new contact or routine add up.
content.assessment.BARC_10.band1.label: Strong recovery capital
content.assessment.BARC_10.band1.descrip: You have a strong base of supports. Keep using them.
content.assessment.SOWS.name: Subjective Opiate Withdrawal Scale
content.assessment.SOWS.purpose: Sixteen symptoms rated right now, to track how opioid withdrawal feels.
content.assessment.SOWS.band0.label: No symptoms
content.assessment.SOWS.band0.descriptio: You are not reporting withdrawal symptoms right now.
content.assessment.SOWS.band1.label: Mild withdrawal
content.assessment.SOWS.band1.descriptio: Mild symptoms. Rest, fluids and distraction can help.
content.assessment.SOWS.band2.label: Moderate withdrawal
content.assessment.SOWS.band2.descriptio: Moderate symptoms. A doctor or pharmacist can advise on medicines that ease withdrawal.
content.assessment.SOWS.band3.label: Severe withdrawal
content.assessment.SOWS.band3.descriptio: Severe symptoms. Please contact a doctor, treatment service or emergency services now.
content.assessment.SAWS.name: Short Alcohol Withdrawal Scale
content.assessment.SAWS.purpose: Ten symptoms rated to track alcohol withdrawal.
content.assessment.SAWS.band0.label: Mild withdrawal
content.assessment.SAWS.band0.descriptio: Mild symptoms. If they get worse, seek medical advice — alcohol withdrawal can become dangerous.
content.assessment.SAWS.band1.label: Higher withdrawal
content.assessment.SAWS.band1.descriptio: Strong symptoms. Alcohol withdrawal can be dangerous: contact a doctor or emergency services now.
content.assessment.CWS.name: Cannabis Withdrawal Scale
content.assessment.CWS.purpose: Nineteen experiences from the last 24 hours, rated 0–10, to track cannabis withdrawal.
content.assessment.CWS.band0.label: Lower
content.assessment.CWS.band0.description: Few or mild symptoms. They usually ease within one to two weeks.
content.assessment.CWS.band1.label: Moderate
content.assessment.CWS.band1.description: Noticeable symptoms. Sleep, exercise and support can help while they pass.
content.assessment.CWS.band2.label: Higher
content.assessment.CWS.band2.description: Strong symptoms. A doctor can help with sleep and mood. If you have thoughts of harming yourself, call a crisis line now. (The CWS has no official cut-offs; these bands are a guide.)
content.assessment.ACSA.name: Amphetamine Cessation Symptom Assessment
content.assessment.ACSA.purpose: Sixteen symptoms rated to track stimulant withdrawal.
content.assessment.ACSA.band0.label: Lower
content.assessment.ACSA.band1.label: Moderate
content.assessment.ACSA.band1.descriptio: Noticeable symptoms. Low mood and tiredness are common and usually ease over a few weeks.
content.assessment.ACSA.band2.label: Higher
content.assessment.ACSA.band2.descriptio: Strong symptoms. Please talk to a doctor. If you have thoughts of harming yourself, call a crisis line or emergency services now. (No official cut-offs; these bands are a guide.)
content.alert.medetomidine.title: Medetomidine in the US fentanyl supply
content.alert.medetomidine.body: In parts of the US, the sedative medetomidine has largely replaced xylazine in street fentanyl. Pennsylvania drug checking found it in about 95% of fentanyl samples in Q2 2025, and Philadelphia in over 70%. Withdrawal from it can be severe and may need hospital care, so get medical help early.
content.alert.xylazine-wounds.title: Xylazine can cause serious wounds
content.alert.xylazine-wounds.body: Xylazine ("tranq") can cause wounds that heal slowly, sometimes away from where you inject. Keep wounds clean and covered, and get medical care for spreading redness, fever or blackened skin. Naloxone does not reverse xylazine, but always give it for a suspected overdose.
content.alert.nitazenes.title: Nitazenes: stronger than fentanyl
content.alert.nitazenes.body: Nitazene opioids have been found in at least 37 countries, in heroin, fake pills and other drugs. Fentanyl strips do not detect them, and nitazene strips miss some types. Use less, go slow, never use alone and keep naloxone close.
content.alert.fentanyl-in-stimulants.bod: Fentanyl is turning up in cocaine, meth and pressed pills, so people who don't use opioids can overdose too. Test if you can, don't use alone and carry naloxone.
content.alert.negative-strip.title: A negative strip doesn't mean safe
content.alert.negative-strip.body: Test strips only look for specific substances and can miss others or give false negatives. Treat every unknown supply with care: start low, go slow and have naloxone and someone with you.
